_comment: Single source of truth for which keyboards the app can identify and load. boards.py reads this to detect the connected board (by VID/PID, plus the optional 'productString' discriminator when several distinct keyboards share one VID:PID), open the right vendor interface (usage_page), load the right layout (keymap), and pick the protocol profile. Add a board here when its layout + identity land; set protocol once its packet format is decoded. VID/PID are hex strings. usage_page null -> device opener falls back to the highest interface. protocol null -> layout/identity only (lighting & actuation disabled until decoded). 'frameLen' — the board's vendor HID frame size in BYTES (omitted -> drivers default to 64, today's wired value). Drivers must size EVERY frame from this field, never hardcode: the MINI 60 HE PRO's 2.4GHz dongle speaks the same protocol at 32-byte frames (payload chunk = frameLen - 8), and a 64-byte frame sent at a 32-byte-report interface is silently truncated by hidapi and reads as 'different protocol' (that exact artifact falsified an earlier dongle probe). boards.py's frozen BoardProfile does not carry the field; drivers/mini60.frame_len_for_profile reads it from this raw JSON by slug (the hostEngineMaxFps passthrough pattern). PER-BOARD DATA BLOCKS (all optional; boards that omit them degrade to safe defaults): 'capabilities' — feature flags, each true | false | 'wip'; 'wip' means the protocol is SOURCE-ONLY (read from vendor driver source, never proven on hardware or in a capture) and the UI must not drive it. Known flags: lighting, actuation, perKeyRgb, rapidTrigger, socd, macros, calibration, gamepad, deadzone. 'lighting' — the board's OWN firmware effect table (id/byte/name + per-mode speed/color/direction rules), slider scales (brightnessMax/speedMax), offModeByte/customModeByte, hostEngine (may the host per-key effects engine stream to this board), hostEngineMaxFps (the board's measured sustainable host-stream rate in frames/second — the effects engine paces to min(its default, this) and the UI reads this ONE field on every board; passed through RAW by app_web._host_engine_max_fps because boards.py's validator whitelists lighting keys), and modeListSource: 'static' (this table is the only truth) or 'hybrid'/'firmware' (the firmware also answers a mode-list query, named in modeQuery). 'actuation' — deadzoneScope ('per-key' | 'global'; global means dead zones live in a whole-board config table and a per-key dead-zone UI CANNOT work), travel/RT/dead-zone ranges in mm, and the board's switch/axis profile list. 'productString' — string or list; USB product strings that positively identify this board among same-VID:PID siblings (at most one entry per VID:PID may omit it; that entry is the fallback match). 'offerInUi' — MAY THE UI OFFER THIS BOARD TO THE USER? An explicit boolean so the fact lives in data instead of being re-derived (differently, and wrongly) at each UI site. It gates OFFERING ONLY — board pickers, the README support table, anything that advertises a board as something you can pick and drive. It NEVER gates identification: detection, layout loading, the connected-board badge and the 'this board is recognised but not driveable yet' explanation all ignore it, because removing an entry from the registry is what would actually break Aether's ability to name the hardware in front of it. The rule the data follows (guarded by tests/test_boards.py::test_offer_in_ui_matches_evidence): offerInUi is true exactly when the board is drivable (protocol wired) AND at least one capability is proven true — a board whose every capability is false or 'wip' has nothing working to offer, so it is identified but never advertised. Omitted -> defaults to the board's `drivable` value, so legacy/test entries degrade safely. Provenance markers used in _note fields: HARDWARE-VERIFIED (round-tripped on the physical board), CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE (matches labeled frames from the vendor driver), SOURCE-ONLY (read from vendor driver source only — must be flagged 'wip', never true). Keep in sync with data/boards.json (the README roadmap table).

boards.name: Aula Win60 HE
boards._note: CAPABILITY PROVENANCE: lighting / actuation / perKeyRgb / rapidTrigger (trigger modes 12/13) / socd (cmd 36 PRCS) / deadzone per-key (cmd 38) / calibration (cmd 33 revise) / gamepad (board cmd 20 sub 3 + host virtual pad) are all HARDWARE-VERIFIED — these are the app's original working paths (CLAUDE.md cheat-sheet, app_web.py). macros = 'wip': the cmd 0x19 macro layout is SOURCE-ONLY (hed driver dec_agreement/deobfuscated.js setMacroValue) — no builders exist and it was never exercised on hardware. PRODUCT-STRING COLLISION: FIVE different keyboards ship with 2E3C:C365 (WIN 60 HE x2 switch kits, WIN 68 HE x2 kits, KP-TE153), disambiguated ONLY by USB product string — vendor list in docs/context/hed-aulacn-raw/driver_src/config__device.json (SOURCE-ONLY): SI2825HEARGB / SI2825KZHEARGB = this 60% board; SI2828HEARGB / SI2828KZHEARGB = WIN 68 HE; SI2851UKKZHEARGB = KP-TE153. This entry claims the two SI2825 strings and stays the FALLBACK when the product string is absent or matches nothing, so detection behaviour is unchanged for existing users. The WIN 68 HE / KP-TE153 siblings now have their own discriminated entries (aula-win68-he, aula-kp-te153) with the vendor's own per-product layouts.
boards._productStringNote: HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-20: this board's real USB product string is 'WIN 60 HE' (read from hid.enumerate() on the physical device). The SI2825* values are the vendor's INTERNAL MODEL CODES from hed.aulacn.com's config/device.json — they were originally declared here on the assumption that device.json's 'product' field was the USB product string. It is NOT. They are kept only as documentation of the model↔board mapping and will never match a real device. Any sibling's SI28xx string below is likewise a model code, not a USB string, and its real USB string is UNVERIFIED (a WIN 68 HE most plausibly reports 'WIN 68 HE' by analogy, but nobody has read one). Unmatched strings fall back to this entry, which is the pre-existing behaviour, so an unrecognised C365 board is no worse off than before.

lighting._note: Firmware cmd-7 mode table, HARDWARE-VERIFIED (CLAUDE.md cheat-sheet), moved verbatim from ui/runtime_src/src/app.jsx FW_MODES. 'frenzy' intentionally shares byte 11 with 'fireworks' (host-engine alias over the same firmware mode). direction kinds: lr | ud | all | rotate | gather (cmd-7 direction bytes right0 left1 up2 down3 spread4 gather5). brightness/speed bytes clamp 0..4 (0 = off). modeListSource 'hybrid': this static table is authoritative, but the firmware also answers readLightList (protocol.build_read_light_list, cmd 10) — usable as a registry validator; nothing calls it yet (SOURCE-ONLY as an app path, exercised on hardware only by the standalone cycle_modes.py tool). hostEngineMaxFps 60: this field means the board's SUSTAINABLE host-stream rate, and 60 is it — effects.py runs at FPS=60 precisely because a 120 bump saturated the USB pipe (8 cmd-9 pages/frame x 120 = 960 HID writes/s) and was reverted on hardware. It was briefly recorded as 120, which was the engine's historical target, not an achievable rate; quoting 120 anywhere also understates what a capped board achieves relative to it. Declared so the UI reads one uniform field on every board; equal to the engine default, so pacing is unchanged.

actuation._note: HARDWARE-VERIFIED (cmd 33): units 0.01 mm; ranges as exposed by the current UI (actuation.jsx) — firmware minimum travel is 0.08 mm per CLAUDE.md, UI uses 0.1. deadzoneScope 'per-key': cmd 38 writes per-key dead bands. Switch profiles feed cmd 37; ids/codes moved verbatim from actuation.jsx SWITCHES + app.jsx handlePickSwitch (hm1=1 hh1=2 cy1=3 tc1=5).

boards.name: Aula WIN 68 HE
boards._note: DISCRIMINATED SIBLING of aula-win60-he: same USB identity 2E3C:C365, identified only by product string. SI2828HEARGB / SI2828KZHEARGB are the two switch-kit variants of the same board; the vendor's key tables for them are byte-identical, so both strings share one layout file. DRIVABILITY DECISION 2026-07-20, from an audit of the vendor driver (docs/context/hed-aulacn-raw/driver_deobf/): protocol 'protocol' because the hed driver serves all five 2E3C:C365 products through ONE protocol code path with ZERO product-string branching at protocol level. Evidence: (a) agreement.deobf.js (the entire packet layer) references curDevice.product exactly once, as a localStorage cache key (line 185); (b) every full-table write is a FIXED-SIZE full-matrix constant, identical for all five products and never sized from key count — keymap 0x210 (132x4, setKeyValue), per-key RGB 0x18C (132x3, setCustomLight), switch table 0x84 (setKeySwitch), dead-band 0x108 (132x2, setDeadBand), trigger select = 22-column bitmask with row bits (setAnyTriggerValue) — so 61 vs 68 keys changes WHICH slots are populated (layout-driven), not framing or sizes; (c) all index math is the same hardcoded 6x22 matrix (row=idx//22, col=idx%22) everywhere; (d) maxTriggerTravel, triggerUnit (raw/100, or raw/1000 when the isHighPrecision bit is set) and the optional-feature set (isDeadBand/isGamePad/isRS/isRKRT bits in the info report, agreement.deobf.js line 31) are NEGOTIATED FROM THE DEVICE at connect, never assumed per product; (e) the per-product quirks that do exist are UI-layer only (KGA75HEARGB DKS route defaults, YC75HEARGB tab skip, 7575US/QK75C fixed-key filters) — none touches command bytes and none applies to this board. This is NOT the shared-VID fallacy: every falsified 'same protocol' inference (80A1 vs 80A2, the FEFE/FEFC dongles, the 38A6 family, the 80B2 alt PID) crossed a DIFFERENT USB identity; here the identity is bit-identical, Aether cannot even distinguish the boards at the transport layer, and the shipping vendor driver drives this exact board through the captured code path in production. CAPABILITY PROVENANCE: the frames are HARDWARE-VERIFIED / CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE via aula-win60-he through this same code path; their applicability to THIS model is SOURCE-ONLY (the invariance audit above) — no WIN 68 has ever been round-tripped by Aether. lighting / actuation / perKeyRgb / rapidTrigger / socd / calibration = true on that shared-identity evidence. deadzone and gamepad = 'wip' because the vendor driver gates them on firmware FEATURE BITS never read from a WIN 68 — do not drive them until the info-report bits are confirmed. Key indices come from the vendor's own per-product table (driver_src/config__keys__SI2828HEARGB.json) — the same source that reproduced the hardware-verified Win60 map exactly — and they DIFFER from the 60% board (R-Shift 101 here vs 100 there). That difference is why this entry must exist: before it, a WIN 68 owner fell back to aula-win60-he and was driven with the WRONG 60% indices. BRING-UP CHECKS on first hardware contact: read max travel (cmd 33 sub 4) to confirm triggerUnit = 0.01 mm (a high-precision firmware would scale actuation values 10x), read the feature bits, and travel-test the non-60% keys to confirm their indices.
boards._productStringNote: ASSUMED, NOT VERIFIED: 'WIN 68 HE' is an analogy from the Win60, whose real USB product string was read from hardware as 'WIN 60 HE' (the SI2828* values are vendor model codes from device.json, not USB strings — see the win60 entry). If a real WIN 68 HE reports something else it falls back to the win60 entry and gets the 60% keymap, i.e. exactly today's behaviour — no regression, but the discriminator simply won't fire until someone reads a real one.

lighting._note: SOURCE-ONLY-SHARED: the Win60's cmd-7 firmware mode table, applied to this sibling because the same driver serves both through one code path and the mode list is ultimately firmware-negotiable (modeListSource 'hybrid': readLightList / cmd 10 can validate this table against the board at bring-up). Never read back from a physical WIN 68.

actuation._note: Ranges mirror the Win60 UI ranges (units 0.01 mm) — but triggerUnit and max travel are DEVICE-NEGOTIATED in the vendor driver (readMaxTriggerTravel + isHighPrecision bit), so confirm them from the board at bring-up before trusting the scale. deadzoneScope 'per-key' is a protocol-family fact (cmd 38 writes a per-key 132x2 table), but the deadzone CAPABILITY itself is 'wip' pending the isDeadBand firmware bit. switches []: this board's switch kits (SI2828 HE vs KZ) were never enumerated — the firmware answers the switch list itself (cmd 37 sub 0), so leave empty until read back.

boards._offerNote: offerInUi false (2026-07-21, user request): 69-key UK ISO variant sharing 2E3C:C365 with the Win60 HE. Its layout is the vendor's own and its protocol is the Win60's, but no KP-TE153 has ever been driven by Aether, and the ISO PRCS hidCode remap (0x31->0x32) leaves SOCD in particular unverified for it. Detected and drawn, not offered.
boards.name: Aula KP-TE153
boards._note: DISCRIMINATED SIBLING of aula-win60-he: same USB identity 2E3C:C365, identified only by product string SI2851UKKZHEARGB. 69-key UK ISO layout (layout type 'uk'). DRIVABILITY: protocol 'protocol' on the same evidence as aula-win68-he (see that entry's audit of docs/context/hed-aulacn-raw/driver_deobf/): the vendor's protocol layer has zero product-string branching, all table writes are fixed-size full-matrix constants never sized from key count, index math is the shared 6x22 matrix, and travel unit + feature set are negotiated from the device — the shipping vendor driver drives this exact board through the identical, capture-confirmed code path. NOT the shared-VID fallacy: all four falsified same-protocol inferences crossed different USB identities; this identity is bit-identical to the hardware-verified Win60. CAPABILITY PROVENANCE: frames HARDWARE-VERIFIED / CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE via aula-win60-he; applicability to this model SOURCE-ONLY (invariance audit); never round-tripped on a physical KP-TE153. lighting / actuation / perKeyRgb / rapidTrigger / calibration = true on that shared-identity evidence. socd = 'wip' — UNLIKE the WIN 68: the ONE layout-dependent protocol nuance found in the audit lands exactly on this board: the vendor's setPrcsData remaps a PRCS key2 hidCode 0x31 -> 0x32 (ANSI backslash -> ISO Non-US #) when curDevice.type !== 'us' (agreement.deobf.js), and nobody has verified that Aether's SOCD path feeds ISO-correct hidCodes for a UK layout — do not drive SOCD until that is checked. deadzone / gamepad = 'wip' pending the firmware feature bits (isDeadBand / isGamePad, never read from this model). macros = 'wip' (SOURCE-ONLY even on the Win60). Key indices from the vendor's own table (driver_src/config__keys__SI2851UKKZHEARGB.json); like the WIN 68 it parts from the 60% map (R-Shift 101 vs 100) — before this entry a KP-TE153 owner was driven with the wrong 60% indices via the fallback. BRING-UP CHECKS: confirm triggerUnit 0.01 mm via cmd 33 sub 4, read the feature bits, travel-test the ISO and non-60% keys to confirm indices.

lighting._note: SOURCE-ONLY-SHARED: the Win60's cmd-7 firmware mode table (same driver, one code path; modeListSource 'hybrid' — validate against the board via readLightList / cmd 10 at bring-up). Never read back from a physical KP-TE153.

actuation._note: Ranges mirror the Win60 UI ranges (units 0.01 mm); triggerUnit and max travel are DEVICE-NEGOTIATED in the vendor driver — confirm from the board at bring-up. deadzoneScope 'per-key' is a protocol-family fact (cmd 38, 132x2 table); the deadzone capability stays 'wip' pending the isDeadBand firmware bit. switches []: kit never enumerated — the firmware answers the switch list (cmd 37 sub 0).

boards.name: Aula Mini 60 HE Pro (wired)
boards._note: The MINI 60 HE PRO over its USB-C CABLE (product string 'KEYBOARD MINI 60 HE PRO'); same physical board as the 0xFEFE dongle entry below. frameLen 64 declared explicitly (CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE, all 457 wired frames) for symmetry with the dongle's frameLen 32 — the 2026-07-20 dongle captures proved the receiver speaks this SAME protocol at half frame size (chunk = frameLen - 8), and the dongle entry is now drivable through the same protocol_mini60/Mini60Driver (see its _note for what is and is not verified wirelessly — notably host streaming does NOT exist over 2.4GHz). Vendor config collection: iface 2 usage_page 0xFF68 usage 0x61 (iface 3 / 0xFF67 rejects writes). DECODED 2026-07-20 from a WebHID capture of the official hub.aulacn.com driver -- see docs/context/issue-6-mini60-pro-raw/ (capture JSON + the driver's own unpacked JS). protocol_mini60 is golden-tested byte-for-byte against all 210 captured OUT frames AND round-trip verified on the physical board: device info (0x10) returns the right VID/PID; lighting mode/brightness/speed written with 0x23 read back correctly via 0x13; a 1.23 mm trip written with 0x27 reads back via 0x17 and the table restores byte-identical. The board's stored records also decode to exactly the values set through the vendor UI (trip 3.00 / RT press 1.25 / RT release 0.75), confirming the record layout from an independent direction. HISTORY WORTH KEEPING: protocol_sonix (the 0x80A1 MINI60HE Max) was the obvious hypothesis -- adjacent PID, same 0xFF68 usage page -- and it was tested on hardware and FALSIFIED. Its frames are acked and ignored because it defaults byte[16] to 0; every real lighting frame sets byte[16]=0x01. It is also BIG-endian where this board is LITTLE-endian. Shared VID, shared usage page, and shared byte order have each been wrong for this board in turn. perKeyRgb is TRUE, verified on hardware 2026-07-20: effect mode 20 (custom) plus a 504-byte SET 0x24 table of 126 x [ledId,r,g,b] round-tripped byte-for-byte through GET 0x14 and restored cleanly. Worth remembering HOW this was nearly missed: the vendor lighting page never sent a per-key table during the capture, so per-key RGB was first written off as unsupported. The capture showed what the UI happened to exercise, not what the firmware accepts -- the SDK source (docs/context/issue-6-mini60-pro-raw/HFD_SDK_DECODE.md) revealed cmd 0x24 and hardware then confirmed it. Absence from a capture is not absence from the firmware. This means Aether's host-driven effects engine (effects.py) CAN drive this board. CAPABILITY PROVENANCE (2026-07-20): lighting TRUE HARDWARE-VERIFIED (0x23 write + 0x13 read-back); actuation TRUE HARDWARE-VERIFIED (0x27 write + 0x17 read-back, byte-identical restore); perKeyRgb TRUE HARDWARE-VERIFIED (mode 20 + 504-byte 0x24 table, all 126 slots round-tripped); rapidTrigger TRUE CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE (labeled RT_PRESS/RT_RELEASE 73-frame write passes) plus the board's stored RT records read back on hardware decode to the vendor-set values (press 1.25 / release 0.75 mm); deadzone TRUE with GLOBAL scope — dead zones live in the 0x11/0x21 game-mode table at payload[8]/[9] (topDeadZone write CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE), NOT per-key: never render a per-key dead-zone control for this board; socd 'wip' SOURCE-ONLY (key-table pageType 11 via SET_KEY 0x22, never captured); macros 'wip' SOURCE-ONLY (0x15/0x25; the capture's macro nav mark has zero frames); calibration 'wip' SOURCE-ONLY (SET_CALIBRATION_ON 100 / OFF 101, CLEAR_CALIBRATION 5); gamepad FALSE — no board-side gamepad command exists anywhere in the HFD SDK. lighting.hostEngine=true, HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-20 by the streaming spike (PER_BOARD_PARITY_PLAN.md section 1 task 7): two different commands write per-key RGB and picking the wrong one was the whole problem — 0x24 is the PERSISTENT flash-backed table at 17.43 ms/write = 6.4 fps (unusable for animation; it remains the 'Per-key Paint' path), while 0x32 SET_GIF_LIGHT_DATA is the LIVE STREAM at 4.00 ms/write = 27.7 fps sustained, zero write errors, p50 36.08 ms / p95 36.13 ms per frame (9 writes of 56 payload bytes each), fire-and-forget with no replies read mid-stream (repeated reads on a persistent handle error on this device; writes-only is what was benchmarked). Frame layout confirmed from the vendor's own gifLight source (HFD_SDK_DECODE.md section 9.3) and exercised on hardware. 0x36 CLEAR_LED_DATA stops/clears. hostEngineMaxFps 28 records the measured ceiling.
boards._advancedKeysNote: socd 'wip' -> TRUE, and the new remap / advancedKeys flags TRUE, on 2026-07-21. EVIDENCE: a full sweep of the vendor app over the 2.4GHz dongle (docs/context/issue-6-mini60-pro-raw/webhid-capture-FULL-SUITE-wireless.json, decoded by analyze_full_suite.py) plus the earlier wired sweep (webhid-capture-macros.json, FULL_APP_CAPTURE_NOTES.md sections 1 and 3) put ALL FIVE advanced-key types and plain remap on the wire as decoded 4-byte records in the SAME 512-byte key table this driver already read-modify-writes for macro binds (0x12 read / 0x22 write, a path that is separately HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-20). The wireless sweep reassembles 504 bytes from 147 0x22 frames and yields: idx 49 and 51 = 0B 03 04 07 (SOCD, mode 3, HID usages A/D), idx 33 and 35 = 0C 00 14 08 (Rapid Snap pair), idx 34 = 08 01 00 00 (DKS slot 1), idx 65 = 0A 00 00 00 (Toggle), idx 66 = 09 00 00 28 (Mod-Tap), idx 84/86 = 02 00 36 00 / 02 00 45 00 (plain remaps). That is a DECODED RECORD, not an inference from the SDK source, so 'wip' (defined in this registry as SOURCE-ONLY) would now misstate the evidence — which is exactly the failure mode the macros flag hit twice. socd is flagged on THIS wired entry as well because the wired board runs the same protocol at 64-byte frames and the wired capture carries the identical pageType-11/12 records; the framing difference is chunk size only. WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN, and must not be claimed: (1) only ONE SOCD mode byte was ever observed (0x03, 'Key 1 Priority' in the wireless sweep; the wired sweep shows 0x02) while the vendor UI offers four modes — the driver takes mode as a caller parameter and validates nothing beyond a byte, because the remaining values are genuinely unknown; (2) the Mod-Tap delay byte (0x28 = 40) has an UNKNOWN unit from a single sample — the wired notes read it as 10 ms units from a different single sample (0x19 = 25 at a UI setting of 250 ms), which is consistent but is still one sample per transport; (3) the DKS and Mod-Tap ACTION slots (which function fires at each travel point / on long vs short press) were never filled in by the vendor UI and their encoding is NOT CAPTURED — this driver writes the record and the DKS travel points only; (4) DKS byte 1 as a slot index is consistent across the two captures (wired slot 0, wireless slot 1) but only one DKS key existed in each, so it is not proven. calibration deliberately stays 'wip': it was never exercised because the vendor app WIPES stored calibration before starting it, and 0x64/0x65 are on the protocol module's NEVER-SEND list.
boards._macrosNote: macros TRUE, HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-21: a 10-event macro composed by OUR encoder (not a replay of a captured vendor frame — varied delays 0..100 ms, H/E/L/L/O HID usages) was written to slot 5 via 0x25, read back byte-for-byte identical via 0x15, and the slot restored to empty. The key-table binding path (0x12 read / 0x22 write, pageType 6) was separately hardware-verified when 11 records were cleared and all 117 others preserved byte-identical. This flag previously read 'wip' from before that verification, which left the driver implementing macros while the capability gate claimed source-only — a cross-board sweep caught the disagreement (list_macros returned instead of raising).

lighting._note: This board's OWN firmware mode list (SET 0x23 / GET 0x13): 0 = lights off, 1 = static, 2..19 = dynamic1..dynamic18, 20 = custom per-key. All 19 dynamic modes plus brightness/speed 0..5 are CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE (labeled frames + 0x13 read-back; BRIGHTNESS_DEC went 5->4 confirming the 0..5 scale). English display names are SOURCE-ONLY from the vendor i18n lightEffectHfd dict (driver_src/index-BZJzwCAk.js) — far better than the Chinglish menu labels. Per-mode control rules from lightDisabled() (driver_src/light-BPRaNowv.js), SOURCE-ONLY except as upgraded below: speed ignored for modes 1 and 20; direction (a 0/1 byte) only meaningful for modes 10, 11, 12, 16 and 18. COLOR FLAGS / colorMode CORRECTION (2026-07-20): 0x23 frame byte [16] is the SDK's colorMode (randomColor ? 1 : 0). It was long recorded as 'must be 1' because every wired-capture frame carried 1 and an early hardware probe sending 0 appeared to no-op — a single-valued sample mistaken for a constant, which meant USER-CHOSEN COLOURS WERE LIKELY IGNORED in fixed-colour modes. The 2.4GHz dongle capture (WIRELESS_DONGLE_FINDINGS.md, transcribed frames — CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE (transcribed)) shows both values correlated exactly with the mode: fixed-colour modes 1/2/4/7 send colorMode 0; multicolour modes 8/15/17/18/19 send 1. Accordingly 'color': false (forced-random; drivers derive colorMode 1) is set on modes 6 and 8 (SOURCE-ONLY, lightDisabled) AND on 15/17/18/19 (CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE (transcribed)); mode 8 is doubly confirmed. Drivers derive byte [16] from this flag via drivers/mini60._color_mode_for; custom mode 20 deliberately keeps the legacy 1 (its HARDWARE-VERIFIED per-key round trip used 1 and no capture shows its colorMode). modeListSource 'static': the HFD SDK has NO firmware mode-list query command — this table is the only source. hostEngine true, HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-20: host animation streams over cmd 0x32 (SET_GIF_LIGHT_DATA, the live channel — NOT the persistent 0x24 table, which is 6.4 fps flash-backed and stays reserved for Per-key Paint) at a measured 27.7 fps sustained with zero write errors; hostEngineMaxFps 28 is that measured ceiling and the effects engine paces to it (its FPS-normalised spawners keep particle density correct at 28).

actuation._note: Record layout CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE + hardware round-trip (write 0x27 / read 0x17: 126 records x 8 bytes, trip/RT LE16 in 0.01 mm). Ranges SOURCE-ONLY from vendor Trigger_Data (driver_src/trigger-t6lqQxHu.js): travel 0.1..3.4 step 0.01 (max capped by the active axis's maxTravel), RT 0.01..3.4, dead zone 0..0.5. deadzoneScope 'global': dead zones live at payload[8]/[9] of the 0x11/0x21 game-mode table (topDeadZone position CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE) — they are whole-board values, NOT per-key; a per-key dead-zone UI cannot work on this hardware. switches []: the 0x27 record has a per-key axisType byte, but this board's axis ids live in the vendor hub's device config (axisMap, driver_src/HFD-D07mGRx8.js) and were never captured — ASSUMED until read back from hardware, so no axis list is declared yet.

boards.name: Aula Mini 60 HE Pro (2.4GHz dongle)
boards._note: The SAME keyboard as aula-mini60he-pro, reached through its 2.4GHz receiver (USB product string 'MINI 60 HE PRO Dongle', read from hardware). A separate entry because the registry keys on VID:PID and the transport genuinely differs. PROTOCOL RESOLVED + DRIVABLE 2026-07-20. Evidence trail (docs/context/issue-6-mini60-pro-raw/: WIRELESS_DONGLE_FINDINGS.md, webhid-capture-dongle-2026-07-20.json, webhid-capture-dongle-handshake.json): the dongle speaks the SAME protocol_mini60 envelope — identical AA header and command set (0x10/0x11/0x12/0x13/0x14/0x17/0x23/0x27 observed wirelessly), identical mode bytes and table geometry (the captured 0x27 pass ends at 0x03D8 + 24 = 0x3F0, the same 1008-byte actuation table) — at HALF the frame size: every frame is 32 bytes, payload chunk = frameLen - 8 = 0x18. TRANSPORT: usage_page 0xFF60 usage 0x61, report id 0, 32-byte reports — HARDWARE-VERIFIED: a raw hidapi handle on that collection gets valid 0x55 replies (0x10/0x12/0x13/0x17), and it is the exact collection the vendor driver holds (navigator.hid.getDevices()). TWO TRAPS COST HOURS TODAY, recorded so nobody repeats them: (1) FRAME SIZE — an early probe sent 64-byte frames, the 32-byte-report interface truncated them (hidapi n=33), nothing answered, and 'different protocol' was wrongly concluded; always size frames from frameLen. (2) CONTENTION + ACCEPTED-BUT-IGNORED — while the vendor web page held the device, raw-handle probes got writes ACCEPTED with no reply (plus a fake zero-error 23.8 fps 0x32 'benchmark' with the keyboard dark, and an earlier fake 4358 fps from a lowest-interface-number pick landing on short-writing 0xFFFF); close the vendor page before probing, and judge success ONLY on a valid 0x55 reply or a visible effect. HARDWARE-VERIFIED over the dongle (visually confirmed): 0x23 lighting mode + colour (static red/blue, Spectrum Cycle), the colorMode byte (static red sent with colorMode 0 rendered FIXED red — independently confirming the byte-16 fix), and the 0x24 persistent per-key table (custom mode + solid green across all 126 keys, 21 chunks of 24 bytes). TRANSPORT PRECEDENCE (HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-21): this dongle only answers while the keyboard is actually running on RF. With the USB-C cable plugged in the board switches to wired mode and the receiver still enumerates but has NOTHING behind it — every read times out (0/42 pages). So when both transports are attached the dongle entry is hollow, which is the concrete reason drivers.connected_profiles must rank the wired entry first; it is not merely a preference for the better link. Any dongle bring-up test must be run with the cable OUT or it will produce a spurious negative. CAPABILITY GATING (rule: true only for commands observed working over the RF bridge): lighting TRUE (HARDWARE-VERIFIED, above); perKeyRgb TRUE (HARDWARE-VERIFIED, above); actuation TRUE — now HARDWARE-VERIFIED (2026-07-21), upgraded from the capture-based judgment call that originally set it: with the cable OUT, Aether's own frames at frame_len=32 read all 42 actuation pages over RF, wrote a 1.77 mm trip, read it back exactly, and restored the table byte-identical. The original reasoning is kept because it was sound: the complete 42-frame 0x27 write pass is CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE over this transport from the vendor UI (a real trip change committed through it), our builders reproduce it byte-for-byte in golden tests, the 0x17 read side answers 0x55 on our own raw handle, and 'wip' is defined in this registry as SOURCE-ONLY which would misstate the evidence; an Aether-side write round-trip is still pending and is the first bring-up check. rapidTrigger TRUE — rides the same capture-confirmed 0x27 records; the record layout is content, not framing, and the firmware behind the bridge is literally the wired board (the 0x10 reply reports 0x80A2 + fw V1.53 over the dongle). deadzone 'wip' — its 0x21 write was NEVER observed over the bridge (only the 0x11 read answers); socd / macros / calibration 'wip' (never exercised wirelessly; calibration additionally rides the NEVER-SEND-adjacent 0x64 family); gamepad FALSE (no board-side command exists in the HFD SDK, same as wired). HOST STREAMING DOES NOT EXIST WIRELESSLY: lighting.hostEngine is FALSE, HARDWARE-VERIFIED negative — 0x32 writes are accepted and silently dropped by the RF bridge (a 15 s sweep at a rock-steady 23.8 fps of no-ops rendered ZERO change), and a capture of the vendor's own app driving effects over the dongle emits ONLY 0x23 + 0x14 (anyStream32: false, anyPerKey24: false — the vendor never streams over 2.4GHz; wireless effects are firmware-side only). drivers/mini60 refuses host_effects on this profile so the effects engine cannot silently no-op. SDK NOTE (SOURCE-ONLY, HFD_SDK_DECODE.md section 14): 0xFEFE is shared by the MINI 60 HE PRO, MINI 68 HE PRO and AULA F75 HE dongles, identified by product-name string — this entry claims 'MINI 60 HE PRO Dongle'; sibling dongle entries must carry their own productString discriminators. BRING-UP CHECKS on next hardware contact: 0x27 write + 0x17 read-back round trip (promotes the pending actuation verification), then a deadzone 0x21 RMW round trip (promotes deadzone from 'wip').
boards._advancedKeysNote: socd 'wip' -> TRUE, and the new remap / advancedKeys flags TRUE, on 2026-07-21 — and this entry is where the evidence actually comes from. The full vendor-app sweep that decoded them was captured OVER THIS 2.4GHz TRANSPORT (docs/context/issue-6-mini60-pro-raw/webhid-capture-FULL-SUITE-wireless.json; analyze_full_suite.py reassembles 504 key-table bytes from 147 0x22 frames at 32-byte framing): SOCD idx 49/51 = 0B 03 04 07 (the identical record in BOTH keys of the pair, mode 0x03), Rapid Snap idx 33/35 = 0C 00 14 08, DKS idx 34 = 08 01 00 00, Toggle idx 65 = 0A 00 00 00, Mod-Tap idx 66 = 09 00 00 28, plain remaps idx 84/86 = 02 00 36 00 / 02 00 45 00. Per the gating rule on this entry — true only for commands observed working over the RF bridge — these are the strongest form of that evidence available short of an Aether-side round trip: the vendor's own app committed real bindings through the bridge and the records decode. Contrast the 0x32 stream, which the bridge ACCEPTS AND DROPS: acceptance is not evidence, but a decoded write pass from the app that owns the board is. UNKNOWNS that stay unknown (see the wired entry's _advancedKeysNote for the full list): only one SOCD mode value (0x03) was ever seen against four in the UI, so mode is a pass-through parameter and the other three are NOT claimed; the Mod-Tap delay byte 0x28 has an unknown unit from one sample; DKS/MT action-slot encodings are NOT CAPTURED; DKS byte 1 as a slot index is consistent but unproven with a single DKS key. calibration stays 'wip' deliberately — the vendor wipes stored calibration before starting it, so it was never exercised on purpose.
boards._macrosNote: macros TRUE over RF, HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-07-21: with the cable OUT, a 10-event macro composed by OUR encoder was written to slot 5 via 0x25 at 32-byte frames, read back byte-for-byte identical via 0x15, and the slot restored to empty. Previously 'wip' on the reasoning that nothing had been exercised wirelessly — true at the time, but the flag outlived the evidence. A cross-board hardware sweep caught it: list_macros returned instead of raising, i.e. the driver implemented a feature the gate still called SOURCE-ONLY. Note this is the OPPOSITE of the 0x32 stream, which the RF bridge accepts and silently drops — capability over this transport has to be tested per command, never inferred from the wired result.

lighting._note: IDENTICAL firmware mode table to aula-mini60he-pro — the dongle is an RF bridge to the same board (0x10 over the dongle reports the wired 0x80A2 identity, fw V1.53). Mode bytes CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE wirelessly for 9 of the 20 modes (transcribed first-session frames: 1/2/4/7 with colorMode 0, 8/15/17/18/19 with colorMode 1); the rest are the same firmware. color:false flags mirror the wired entry (modes 6/8 SOURCE-ONLY from lightDisabled(); 15/17/18/19 CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE (transcribed)) — drivers derive 0x23 byte[16] colorMode from this flag. hostEngine FALSE is a HARDWARE-VERIFIED NEGATIVE, not an unmeasured default: the RF bridge accepts 0x32 stream writes and silently drops them (23.8 fps of zero-error no-ops, keyboard dark), and the vendor's own app never streams over 2.4GHz (its wireless effects capture contains only 0x23/0x14). No hostEngineMaxFps is declared — there is no stream to cap.

actuation._note: Same table, same records, same firmware as the wired entry — only the frame paging differs (42 x 0x18 chunks, CONFIRMED-BY-CAPTURE in the dongle 0x27/0x17 sweeps). Ranges SOURCE-ONLY from vendor Trigger_Data, as on the wired entry. deadzoneScope 'global' is a firmware fact (0x11/0x21 table), transport-independent — but the deadzone CAPABILITY is 'wip' here because no 0x21 write was ever observed over the RF bridge. switches [] for the same reason as wired (axis ids never captured).

boards._statusNote: supported since 2026-07-21. Was 'bringup' while only the vendor's own frames had been seen over RF; every capability this entry advertises has since been round-tripped by Aether's own code against the physical receiver with the cable OUT: device info (0x10), lighting write + read-back (0x23/0x13), the full 42-page actuation table (0x27/0x17, a 1.77 mm trip written, read back, table restored byte-identical), the persistent per-key table (0x24), and macros (0x25/0x15). What stays gated is gated on evidence, not on doubt about the transport: host effects are FALSE because the RF bridge accepts 0x32 stream writes and silently drops them, and deadzone/socd/calibration remain 'wip' because they were never exercised across the bridge.
